reading.title: Choosing and storing equipment
reading.text: Maya compares a DSLR camera and mirrorless camera, asking about their different mirror systems. A lens focuses light; a wide-angle lens and telephoto lens give different views. Omar puts a tripod beside a monopod and checks the camera strap. Maya covers an unused lens with its lens cap before putting it in the camera bag. The club then compares flash, softbox and umbrella light, followed by ring light and reflector. They discuss purposes rather than assuming body shape alone proves camera type. The participants agree before photographing one another.

reading.title: Understanding the terms before changing settings
reading.text: Omar compares a camera and light box, then asks about aperture. The opening admits light, while shutter speed concerns capture duration. ISO affects brightness and noise; focus concerns sharpness at the chosen distance. Exposure refers to recorded light. White balance concerns color rendering, and zoom changes the view or magnification. Maya compares wide angle with the decision to edit and crop an image. She asks before retouching personal features. Print produces a paper copy, and a frame supports or borders it. The account explains concepts rather than claiming one setting guarantees a good photograph.

reading.title: Selecting work for a portfolio
reading.text: Maya selects her own photographs for a portfolio. She wants a small collection that shows the range and quality of her work. Omar asks whether the gallery will display them on a wall or online. Maya confirms permission for any recognizable people before sharing and explains important edits. In this account, portfolio is a collection of work, while gallery is the display or place displaying it. Neither term is a promise that every picture is original, licensed or suitable for public use without checking.
